Keep myself busy: exercise, achieve 100% completion in games, read up people's various thoughts online, cleaning the house, finding better ways to network up my devices, ride my electric scooter and pretend that I'm Batman... you know... busy stuff.
I just get really active with my hobbies.

There are quite a few things I do. Call a friend. Write a short story. Paint a picture. Read something. Play the guitar. Take a nap. Go for a run. When I'm home or in a hotel as long as I have background noise I don't really get lonely. Doesn't matter if it's the tv, half the time I don't know what is even playing and volume is pretty low, or if it's music. Just as long as there is some racket to keep me from getting inside my own head.

If I'm looking for a short term solution and can't find anyone to talk to, I usually watch Let's Plays or vlogging video's on Youtube. It makes me feel like someone is talking to me while I work on a hobby to distract me.

A somewhat more longterm solution for me was getting a cat. His company has helped me immensly and I've been feeling significantly less lonely and depressed since the little furball has been walking through the house.

The feeling isn't gone, but these things sure do help!

What you definitely should NOT do is some coping mechanism that damages you, like drinking or overeating. Being lonely is temporary, damage to your body is permanent. Plus, the more overweight you get and the more you rely on alcohol, the worse your mental health will be, which will feed the problem.

For me, a short term fix was ibuprofen (obviously following dosage instructions, warnings, etc.) Seriously. I read a study that showed that NSAIDS helped ease the pain of social rejection, and I found it really took the edge off the loneliness. Maybe it was a placebo, I guess, but it worked for me when I was so lonely I was just lying in bed crying.

More long-term, it helped me to make myself a nice place to live. When I look around my apartment decorated just the way I like it, and I know that I have everything I need and that I am taking care of myself, it makes me feel proud of the life I built and not so sad about being alone, because I don't feel ashamed of myself and I'm glad to be in my own company.

I force myself to go out and partake in adventures. It's not easy because it's actual work forcing myself out the door some days, but I do force myself. When I go hiking, backpacking, kayaking, paragliding, etc, I always document it with my camera and iPhone. At the end of the year, I make annual slideshows and videos for the family, none of whom live nearby.

Personally, I think it's the exposure to new things and experiencing new things that lessens the loneliness. I'm a 41 year old male, and a self-proclaimed "failed heterosexual". I've never been married, have no kids, am living on my own, and gainfully employed in a good job. I've accepted that there aren't any "white picket fences" in my future, nor are there any "happily ever afters". Accepting that is one of the hardest things I've had to do, but it's a realization that had to be made. Now I choose to force myself on adventures and experience new things, even though I'm alone 99% of the time, and know that there's no one at home waiting for me.

I wish I had more to offer you, but adventure is the one thing that's kept me out of a pine box at an earlier age.
